title: Confocal Evaluation of Carbon Quantum Dots Obtained by Microwave Synthesis from Coffee and Garlic Residues
content: Nanotechnology has revolutionized understanding and manipulating matter at the nanometric level [1]. Among the most studied nanomaterials, carbon quantum dots are a promising material in this field due to their unique properties and versatility [2]. However, the syntheses for obtaining these nanomaterials generate a lot of polluting waste. Therefore, the ecological principles in nanoscience for obtaining nanostructured materials focus on environmentally friendly methods and reducing the environmental footprint of nanomaterial development [3]. One of the most environmentally friendly methods is green synthesis through microwaves using precursor materials such as carbon-rich organic compounds (biopolymeric residues), which are subjected to chemical or thermal treatment to generate the nanoscale dots. Controlling the reaction conditions, such as temperature, reaction time, and the presence of stabilizing agents, the size and shape of the dots can be achieved in this bottom-up approach with enhanced optical and electronic properties [4]. This study reveals the uses of an alkaline-based solution with residue as coffee husk and garlic skin from household sources to obtain quantum dots with fluorescence behavior that can be used in bioimaging.
